checks.name: scope-boundary
checks.summary: Scope boundary for V2-086, recorded against base commit a0622910d493cadd94c6d819690dbab0232a44ab on branch v2-task/V2-086, BEFORE any source file was edited: this record's first commit contains rows 1-5 and the whole A1/A2 baseline, and `git status --porcelain` at that commit showed ONLY .agents/v2/evidence paths, so every non-test and test source file named below was still byte-identical to the base. ROW 1 -- what this task makes true: the scheduler becomes a role a real caller can be. internal/application gains exactly one exported constructor, LoopCaller(subject string) (Caller, error), which is the only sanctioned producer of a Caller carrying RoleScheduler and refuses an empty or whitespace-only subject with ErrUnauthenticated; internal/api's CombinedAuthenticator gains one field, SchedulerIdentity, checked AFTER the byte-unchanged runner-session branch and parseIAPEmail but BEFORE the OwnerEmails lookup, and refusing outright an identity configured as both scheduler and owner; POST /internal/reconcile keeps its own identity check byte-for-byte and additionally carries application.LoopCaller(ReconcileIdentity) on the context it hands InternalReconcile; cmd/control-plane/main.go sets SchedulerIdentity from the same strings.ToLower(reconcileIdentity) value it already passes as ReconcileIdentity, adding no environment variable; and internal/runner.Orchestrator's fabricated Caller{Role: RoleOwner, Subject: runner-local-owner} literal is replaced by a required injected field that fails closed when its Role or Subject is empty. The measured before/after is a count: non-test producers of a RoleScheduler Caller 0 -> 1, and reachability of domain.ActorTypeLoop for Requirement.RequestedBy through a transport false -> true. ROW 2 -- what it deliberately does not do: application.RoleScheduler is not removed and no callerActor role pair changes; no operation becomes scheduler-only; no route's role gate changes; no PermitKind, ActorType, Role or status is added; internal/domain is byte-unchanged; contracts/openapi/openapi-v1.yaml is byte-unchanged (sha256 ca62ef4c0e1f7dbe357d03209d68f387581ed53aeaa66b0ea8fc5b8b7eea8cdd before and after) and contracts_changed is empty; api.Config gains and loses no field; POST /internal/reconcile is NOT re-routed through h.config.Authenticator, because that branch runs before the authenticator-nil guard and must keep working under LocalOwnerBearerAuthenticator, which cannot resolve an IAP email at all; LocalOwnerBearerAuthenticator is not changed and no preview-local scheduler environment variable is added; internal/application/readmodels.go, internal/web/**, docs/** and contracts/** are untouched, because actor_type 'loop' is already declared in the RequestedBy schema and already admitted by domain.validActorType, so the new value flows through every existing response and export with no field and no branch; ci/components.json, Makefile, go.mod, go.sum and devbox.* are untouched because the design creates and removes no import edge; no existing test is deleted, renamed or weakened. ROW 3 -- what it records but does not fix: (a) the openapi document declares at contracts/openapi/openapi-v1.yaml lines 5-8 that increment decomposition/planning 'remains a loop scheduler responsibility' while internal/application/service.go's Plan (:888) and Prepare (:1023) accept RoleOwner and 23 test files call one of the two, so the declaration and the application-layer role pair disagree; that is a statement about the public HTTP surface, where neither command has a route at all, and it is recorded here for the tech_lead rather than resolved. (b) Orchestrator.RunFakeJourney has no non-test caller in the repository and cmd/runner/main.go constructs no Orchestrator, so the whole Capture-to-AcceptResult driver is exercised only by internal/runner/orchestrator_test.go; moving the driver into a _test.go file is a larger and better change that is NOT taken here, and is recorded so a later task can decide. (c) the in-memory adapter never trues up its quota reservation, so quota.ReadTransactionUsage (Reads 6001, Writes 1) admits only four READ transactions per budget day against quota.DefaultBudget's 25000 reads; the new proof works around it by stepping an injected clock, never by weakening an assertion, and the adapter defect stays V2-087's. (d) internal/store/firestore's suite prints ok while producing 26 '--- SKIP' lines with no emulator (MEASURED 26, and the coordinator's brief said 49), so that package's run measured nothing about this change; it is recorded under gate rule G7 and never counted as a pass. (e) A6 asks both that the process 'fail to start' when RECONCILE_IDENTITY is also in OWNER_EMAILS and that nothing else in cmd/control-plane/main.go change and that the refusal be asserted through the authenticator; the two halves conflict, so the refusal is implemented and tested in CombinedAuthenticator.Authenticate (every IAP-authenticated request is refused with a message naming the conflict) and NO start-time guard was added -- recorded as a partial, escalated to the tech_lead, not reinterpreted. ROW 4 -- what only a later task can establish: the loop caller the reconcile branch now carries is verified as present and correctly attributed but is NOT consumed by any command inside the tick, because both reconcilers the cmd/control-plane closure drives (reconciler.Reconciler.Tick and reconciler.VerificationReconciler.Tick) take no Caller; the Requirement transitions that will consume it belong to the V2-084 follow-on. The preview-local composition can produce an owner and a runner but not a scheduler. ROW 5 -- this task passes no release gate: exactly three evidence records are issued (application, api, runner), release_eligible is false in all three and in the index, no capability id is cited anywhere, contracts/release-contract/** is untouched, .agents/v2/evidence/V2-022-release-live-dogfood.json is untouched, no release BundleDigest moves, no Provider CLI was started and no Google Cloud resource was touched.

checks.name: a1-baseline-transport-producers
checks.summary: A1(ii) for the api component, MEASURED at a0622910d493cadd94c6d819690dbab0232a44ab and AGREEING with the Work Order on all four line numbers. internal/api/auth.go produces exactly four role-bearing Callers and no others: :50 `application.Caller{Role: application.RoleRunner, Subject: runnerID, RunnerID: runnerID}` in CombinedAuthenticator; :59 `application.Caller{Role: application.RoleOwner, Subject: email}` in CombinedAuthenticator, after the OwnerEmails lookup; :85 the RoleRunner producer in LocalOwnerBearerAuthenticator; :99 the RoleOwner producer in LocalOwnerBearerAuthenticator. BearerAuthenticator (auth.go:16-28) produces nothing of its own: it returns whatever Caller its map holds, which is how the existing tests reach RoleScheduler today and why the defect is invisible from inside the test suite. No RoleScheduler producer exists in internal/api at the base commit.

checks.name: a1-baseline-reconcile-branch-and-its-negatives
checks.summary: A7 baseline, MEASURED at a0622910d493cadd94c6d819690dbab0232a44ab, with two DISAGREEMENTS. The /internal/reconcile branch is internal/api/api.go:99-111 (the Work Order cites api.go:87-92 for the identity check and api.go:113-116 for the authenticator-nil guard; measured, the identity check is the single if at :101 with its 401 at :102, and the `h.config.Authenticator == nil || h.config.Service == nil` guard is at :128-131, so both citations are stale by +12 and +15). sha256 of api.go lines 99-111 at the base commit is ad63e9277f4cc0db9e89276dfd35394e66234e03dcd89a0cba7df621d0e27f28, and sha256 of the identity check alone (lines 99-104) is 3bd6a7c9e3414fa1248f892c549fffa6eee994ac51644c2cc2955ae7e411eb32; the second digest is the one A7 requires to be unchanged after the repair. Second disagreement: the Work Order says the two existing negative cases are at internal/api/api_test.go:85 and :93. Measured, there is ONE test function, TestInternalReconcileRequiresDedicatedIAPIdentity at api_test.go:84, and it contains one POSITIVE case (asserted at :91-93, expecting 202 with the hook called) and one NEGATIVE case (asserted at :100-102, a runner-session header expecting 401 with the hook not called); api_test.go:85 is `called := false` and :93 is a closing brace. The other reconcile negatives live in the V2-083 pin table (api_test.go:3822, :3825, :3826, :3829, :3832, :3835): reconcile-with-nothing-configured 401, reconcile-without-the-scheduler-identity 401, reconcile-with-a-runner-session-header 401, reconcile-with-a-foreign-identity 401, reconcile-accepted 202, reconcile-rejects-get 405. All eight rows are the ones that must keep their exact status codes.

checks.name: a1-baseline-route-role-gates
checks.summary: A10 baseline, MEASURED at a0622910d493cadd94c6d819690dbab0232a44ab: the complete list of transport role gates, so 'no route's role gate changes' is a comparison and not a claim. Owner-only: api.go:138 POST /v1/runner/enrollment, :168 GET /v1/requirements, :181 GET /v1/controls, :194 GET /v1/requirements/{id}, :208 GET /v1/repositories, :221 GET /v1/repositories/{id}, :245 GET /v1/queue/summary, :266 GET /v1/runners, :290 GET /v1/providers, :303 GET /v1/export, :324 GET /v1/release/state, :363 POST /v1/repositories, :393 POST /v1/repositories/{id}:retire, :452 POST /v1/requirements/{id}:answer-input. Runner-only: :373 POST /v1/runner/permits:check, :403 POST /v1/repositories/{id}:observe. Runner-or-scheduler: :439 POST /v1/requirements/{id}:request-input. Owner-or-scheduler: :475 POST /v1/requirements/{id}:start-framing. Ungated at the route and gated by callerActor inside the command: POST /v1/requirements (:360), POST /v1/controls (:368), POST /v1/runner/claims:acquire, /v1/executions/result, /v1/runner/heartbeat, /v1/runner/checkpoints, /v1/leases/{id}:renew, /v1/executions/{id}:start. Note for A9(d): POST /v1/repositories is OWNER-ONLY AT THE TRANSPORT (api.go:363) even though application.RegisterRepository accepts owner|scheduler (repository.go:133), so a scheduler is refused there by the route, which is exactly the 403 A9(d) asks for; and GET /v1/requirements/{id} is owner-only (api.go:194), so the A9 read of the loop-captured Requirement must be performed AS THE OWNER.
